title: Prepare a clearer MOSAIC website and comprehension test
description:
Prepare a reviewable, clearer MOSAIC website and comprehension-test design under the [approved plan](/SHE/issues/SHE-1#document-plan).

Owner: Chief of Staff, with The Oracle validating MOSAIC accuracy. Hard dependency: [knowledge baseline](/SHE/issues/SHE-2). This separate task has a different owner and substantial website/test deliverables. Begin when that baseline is complete; parent nesting is traceability only.

Deliver documents and a reviewable prototype on this task:
- Current-site clarity audit of https://groundstoact.com/, based on actual inspection.
- Proposed information structure and key-page copy explaining what MOSAIC is, who it helps, how it works, a concrete example and a useful next action.
- A reviewable page prototype; obtain repository/source access if needed, while completing independent copy and test work.
- Five-question quiz with answer key, an explanation rubric and a ten-person testing protocol.
- Source-linked Oracle accuracy review of framework claims before final handoff. Coordinate review within these approved tasks without creating additional unapproved issues.

Acceptance: artifacts are inspectable; key claims trace to the reviewed knowledge baselin

title: Establish the MOSAIC knowledge base
description:
Establish SHERIDAN+BAIRNS' authoritative MOSAIC knowledge baseline under the [approved plan](/SHE/issues/SHE-1#document-plan).

Owner: The Oracle. Can start now: hire is active and source inventory can begin with https://groundstoact.com/ and accessible company materials. This is a separate task because it belongs to the MOSAIC curator and supplies a hard knowledge dependency for the website work.

Deliver documents on this task:
- Source register with URLs or file references, dates, versions and provenance.
- Versioned core reference separating established MOSAIC principles, supporting evidence, inference, proposed extensions and unresolved founder-intent questions.
- Plain-language glossary, worked example, FAQ and open-question log.
- An explicit inventory of missing source access; do not invent missing framework details.

Preserve the founder's framework; do not silently redefine it. Request genuinely necessary missing material through a saved question card and in_review. Use existing public sources first. Present the baseline for founder review through a real interaction before treating disputed content as authoritative. Chief of Staff owns coordination and the downstream webs

title: Paperclip onboarding
description:
This is the user's first task in Paperclip. Your job is to understand what they want and propose a path forward. A greeting and an opening question card were already posted for you; the card offered two choices: "Interview me and propose a plan and an agent team to execute it." (option `interview`) or "I have a task in mind" (option `task`, with a text field). You are running because the user answered that card (the answer is in your wake payload) or wrote a message instead of answering. Don't re-introduce yourself and don't post the opening card again.

Work in this order.

1. Take the path the user picked.

   - `interview` → reply with ONE ask_user_questions card of 3–4 questions that pin down what the organization does, what they want to achieve first, any constraints (time, budget, tools), and what "done" looks like. Don't guess; ask. Don't post anything else before the card. The answers lead to the plan-and-team path in step 2.

   - `task` → the text they typed is the task. If it is clear enough to propose on, go straight to step 2. If not, reply with ONE ask_user_questions card of 2–3 questions specific to their message (concrete goal, constraints, what "done" looks like),
